entry.question:
## Physical scenario

Blood contains positive and negative ions and thus is a conductor. A blood vessel, therefore, can be viewed as an electrical wire. We can even picture the flowing blood as a series of parallel conducting slabs whose thickness is the diameter \( d \) of the vessel moving with speed \( v \).

## Question

If you expect that the blood will be flowing at 15\,\text{cm/s} for a vessel 5.0\,\text{mm} in diameter, what strength of magnetic field will you need to produce a potential difference of 1.0\,\text{mV}?

## Answer choices

- A: A: 13.2T

- B: B: 1.32T

- C: C: 0.013T

- D: D: 0.00013T

## Figure caption (auxiliary; use the image as primary evidence)

The image shows a cylindrical rod moving through a magnetic field. Here are the details:

- The cylinder is depicted in red and is oriented horizontally.
- Blue "X" symbols indicate the direction of the magnetic field \(\vec{B}\), which is directed into the page.
- An arrow labeled \(v\) in green indicates the velocity of the cylinder, pointing to the right.
- The diameter of the cylinder is labeled as \(d\).
- The magnetic field \(\vec{B}\) is represented by a vector above the cylinder, with the symbol \(\vec{B}\) placed near it.

The scene illustrates the interaction of the cylinder with the magnetic field as it moves horizontally.
